description: A slender evergreen tree 8-12 m tall with a conical crown, glossy lanceolate leaves rich in oil glands, and clusters of small buds at the branch ends. The unopened, nail-shaped, rose-pink flower buds are picked and dried to give cloves.
cultural_significance: Cloves are a major Indian spice and a flavour of garam masala and paan. The spice was once so valuable that the Maluku (Spice) Islands drew centuries of trade and colonial rivalry.
habitat: Humid tropical island and coastal climates; native to the Maluku Islands of Indonesia and grown in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

uses.title: Toothache and oral health
uses.detail: Clove or its oil is traditionally applied near an aching tooth and used as a mouth freshener (Mukhashodhana).

uses.title: Cough, cold and sore throat
uses.detail: Chewing a clove or taking a decoction with honey is traditional for cough and throat irritation; described as Kaphahara.

uses.title: Nausea and indigestion
uses.detail: Described as Deepana and Pachana; also used for thirst and vomiting (Trishna and Chhardi) in classical texts.

uses.title: Dental analgesic
uses.detail: Eugenol is used in dentistry as a temporary analgesic and antiseptic.

uses.title: Headache relief (external paste)
uses.detail: Paste of cloves is traditionally applied on the forehead; avoid contact with eyes.

preparations.name: Lavanga churna (powder)
preparations.method: Grind dried buds into a powder.
preparations.note: Used in Lavangadi vati and formulations for cough.

preparations.name: Lavangadi vati
preparations.method: Classical lozenge made from clove and other herbs.
preparations.note: Traditionally sucked for throat irritation and cough.

preparations.name: Clove oil (Lavanga taila)
preparations.note: Strong; apply only diluted and in small amounts.

precautions: Clove oil is concentrated and can burn the gums, skin and mucous membranes; it can be toxic if swallowed in large amounts, especially for children. Eugenol may slow blood clotting, so use caution with anticoagulants and before surgery. May lower blood sugar. Avoid medicinal quantities in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

cultivation.sunlight: Partial shade when young, full sun later
cultivation.propagation: Seeds raised in nurseries; slow to flower (6-8 years)
cultivation.harvest: Hand-pick buds when they turn pinkish and sun-dry until dark brown

fun_fact: A clove is an unopened flower bud; if left to bloom it would produce small pink-white flowers.

regions.name: Indonesia (Java, Sumatra & Maluku)
regions.note: Native to the Maluku Islands; Indonesia is a top producer

regions.name: East Africa
regions.note: Zanzibar and Pemba are famous clove islands

regions.name: Tamil Nadu Plains
regions.note: Grown in hill plantations such as Kanyakumari
